## SECURITIES AND FUTURES COMMISSION

12th Floor, Edinburgh Tower, The Landmark, 15 Queen's Road Central, Hong Kong

## 18 December 2002

## Circular to SFC's Registered Intermediaries and Exempt Persons which are not Authorized Institutions

Compliance under the Securities and Futures Ordinance (Cap. 571)

As you are aware, the Securities and Futures Ordinance ('SFO') is targeted to commence on 1 April 2003.  Upon commencement of the SFO, you will be deemed to be a corporation licensed for certain type(s) of regulated activity for a transitional period of two years.  The type(s) of regulated activity that you will be so deemed correspond to those activities that you are carrying out under your current registration or exempt status.

As provided under the  SFO,  you  may  continue  to  carry  on  your  existing  business  of  regulated activities during the transitional period without taking any action on your part.  However, you will need to apply for migration to the new regime if you intend to continue such business beyond the transitional period.  We recommend that you prepare early and submit your application around, if not before, your first anniversary date during the transitional period.  A detailed guideline relating to transitional arrangements will be issued early next year.

You are reminded that except for those provisions of the SFO noted below, all other provisions including the subsidiary legislation, codes and guidelines applicable to licensed persons will be effective upon the commencement of the SFO and will apply with full force and without exception to you and your conduct of regulated activities.  It is important therefore that you apprise yourself now of the changes under the new regime, and make preparation forthwith to ensure compliance with all applicable requirements on 1 April 2003.

- Schedule  10  to  the  SFO  provides  that  during  the  transitional  period,  existing  registrants which  are  deemed  to  be  licensed  corporations  under  the  SFO  are  also  deemed  to  have complied with the requirements on the appointment of responsible officers under sections 125(1)(a) and (b).
- That Schedule further provides that such requirements relating to responsible officers and the  requirements  for  approval  of  substantial  shareholders  under  section  131(1)  are  not applicable to existing exempt persons (which are not authorized institutions) deemed to be licensed corporations during the transitional period.
- The Securities and Futures (Financial Resources) Rules contain transitional provisions that investment  advisers  and  exempt  persons  (which  are  not  authorized  institutions)  are  not required  to  comply  with  the  new  financial  resources  requirements  in  the  first  6  months after the SFO commences.  However, during that 6-month period, investment advisers are still required to comply with the requirements on net tangible assets as provided under the current Financial Resources Rules.

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

The SFC website (www.hksfc.org.hk) contains useful information on the new regime and links to the SFO and its subsidiary legislation gazetted.  We are pleased to advise also that in January 2003, we  will  be  organizing  two  workshops,  one  in  English  and  the  other  in  Chinese,  to  assist  the industry in understanding the new regime and the provisions thereunder.  Announcements will be made regarding these workshops in the coming week through FinNet.

Should  you  have  any  queries,  please  do  not  hesitate  to  contact  your  responsible  Intermediaries Relationship Manager of the Licensing Department.
